world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Anson, G. M. 1972. Description synchronique d'un parler Ewe: Le Watyi; also Capo 1991 A Comparative Phonology of Gbe (De Gruyter, paywalled). Neither readable online.

sources.citation: Faton, Gabriele R. 2018. Waci Speakers in Togo and Benin: A Sociolinguistic Survey. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2018-003. Dallas: SIL International. iii+42 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Purely sociolinguistic; sec. 6.1 (pp. 13-14) only says Waci varieties 'differ slightly in vocabulary, pronunciation, tone, and intonation'. Sec. 2 and Appendix D list the descriptive works (Capo 1977 memoire; Lokossa & Capo 1978; Capo & Codjo n.d. ms on tonal morphemes in Wacigbe and Gengbe).

sources.citation: Hamberger, Klaus. 2011. 'Note sur la transcription des termes ouatchi.' In: La parente vodou: organisation sociale et logique symbolique en pays ouatchi (Togo). Paris: CNRS Editions / Editions de la MSH (OpenEdition Books, doi 10.4000/books.editionsmsh.1200).
sources.note: Anthropologist's transcription note: Ouatchi 'est un dialecte oriental de l'ewe'; Ewe has two tones (haut, bas) with rising, falling and mid realizations; no mention of accent or stress. Page is behind an Anubis JS wall by automated download, read via direct download only.

sources.citation: Capo, Hounkpati B. C. (ed. K. K. Prah). 2000. The New Ewe Orthography: Based on the Gbe Uniform Standard Orthography (GUSO). Cape Town: CASAS. (archive.org item 'ewe-orthography', scanned text)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress; 'accent' occurs only as the name of tone diacritics (accent aigu = high tone etc.); Waci is listed among the GUSO member lects. Orthography manual for Ewe, not a description of Waci.

sources.citation: Lokossa, Augustine A. & Hounkpati B. C. Capo. 1978. Precis grammatical du gengbe et du wacigbe [Wlon gbea adodoi]. Kome/Cotonou: Sous-Commission des langues waci et gen. 47 pp.

sources.note: Short grammar of Gen and Waci; may open with an orthography/tone note. Glottolog editors hold a scan (hh:); SUDOC lists a print copy.

sources.citation: Capo, Hounkpati B. C. & K. Codjo. n.d. An exploration of some tonal morphemes in Wacigbe and Gengbe. Unpublished manuscript (cited in Faton 2018, Appendix D).

sources.note: Only known work specifically on Waci prosody (tone); unpublished.

sources.citation: Capo, Hounkpati B. Christophe. 1991. A Comparative Phonology of Gbe, ch. 2 'Synchronic phonetic setting' (pp. 19-62). Publications in African Languages and Linguistics 14. Berlin/New York: Foris.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Authoritative pan-Gbe phonology with Waci among the sampled lects; ch. 2 covers syllable and tone. Google Books search suggests it is silent on word stress apart from a loanword-tone remark (p. 22), but the chapter should be read to confirm and to quote its tone statement.

sources.citation: Capo, Hounkpati B. C. 1986/1988. Renaissance du gbe, une langue de l'Afrique occidentale: reflexions critiques et constructives sur l'eve, le fon, le gen, l'aja, le gun, etc. Lome: Universite du Benin (1986) / Hamburg: Helmut Buske (1988). ISBN 9783871188473.

sources.note: Capo's French overview of Gbe (based on his dissertation) with a phonological characterization of each cluster incl. Waci in the Ewe cluster; a general remark on 'accent'/tone typology is plausible here.

sources.note: Google Books search-inside (saved by the Gen sibling run): 'stress' has only 2 hits in the whole book - p. 22, English loans whose 'stressed final syllable carry a falling tone' (tea, doctor, key, cocoa, school), and p. 206 bibliography; 'accent' 0 hits. So the tone chapter apparently contains no word-stress rule for Gbe/Waci. Full text paywalled (De Gruyter 405/could not be reached by automated download).
